By whom [is he protected], the Lord of the World, the Protector, the Bodhisattva, the Son of the Conqueror,
the Sovereign of all phenomena, the glorious Āryāvalokiteśvara?
Beholding those beings who were sinful, wicked, suffering, and dwelling in hell,
he was impelled by great compassion through his gaze of mercy.
Having indeed rescued them all, awakened them, and rejoiced with them,
and having established them on the path to enlightenment, he sends them to the abode of the Victors.
Having set out for Sukhāvatī while emitting rays of merit,
he has arrived here to illuminate the world of living beings.
This radiance of his merit, which purifies evil,
has been extended forth, illuminating the entire world and bringing it purification.
Thus, he is the sovereign of all worlds, bearing the purpose of their welfare.
Having personally perceived [the truth] everywhere, he proceeds, delivering all beings.
Beholding even those sinners who were submerged everywhere in the hells and undergoing extreme suffering, he emitted rays of merit toward them.
Having illuminated them, brought them to happiness, uplifted and awakened them,
and established them on the path to enlightenment, he sends them to Sukhāvatī.
Thus that repository of glorious qualities, the bestower of the bliss of the true Dharma,
day by day uplifts and awakens immeasurable beings.
Having established them on the path to enlightenment and caused them to hear the well-spoken Dharma,
he makes all their intentions pure and sends them to Sukhāvatī.
Thus, his great merit is vast, surpassing all the worlds;
it is immeasurable, incalculable, and the means for accomplishing the state of perfect enlightenment.
Even by all the lords of sages, that great and most excellent merit can never be measured or fully enumerated.
For all Buddhas as well, such supreme merit exists,
immeasurable and incalculable, and never otherwise.
No one else is seen to possess such exceedingly great merit;
therefore, he shines forth as the Lord of the Three Worlds in every direction.
Thus, his great merit is immeasurable and most abundant;
indeed, it cannot be measured even by all the lords of sages.
Therefore, this glorious Āryāvalokiteśvara is the Lord of the World, the Teacher of the World, the Master of the World, and the Sovereign of all realms.
Born from the self of the Primordial Buddha, he is the Lord of the World, the Great Lord;
the creator of the universe, the sustainer of the three worlds, and the sun of the knowledge of perfect awakening.
He is always honored and saluted by all the lords of the worlds, by the gods, asuras, yakṣas, kinnaras, rākṣasas, garuḍas, and nāgas.
With all the planets and hosts of stars, with the vidyādharas of great supernatural power,
with the siddhas, sādhya-s, rudras, kumbhāṇḍas, and mahoragas;
And also by all the lords of beings, together with Agni, Yama, and the Maruts;
and by all the Apsarases, and by all the hosts of divine maidens and the like.
Thus, having always meditated upon, recollected, praised, and bowed down to him, he was worshipped by hosts of daughters of the Dānavas, Nāga-lords, Yakṣas, and others.
He was praised, saluted, and worshipped by all the Bhairavas, as well as by all the Mahākāla gaṇas and all the Mātṛkās.
And by all the hosts of ḍākinīs, by all the bhūtas and piśācas, and by all the lords of obstacles, together with the pretas, kaṭhapūtakas, and pūtakas.
And by all the hosts of Māras dwelling within the triple world,
he is constantly and eternally recollected, prostrated to, and praised.
Thus, it is constantly remembered and saluted by all the great ṛṣis, as well as by yogins, ascetics, renunciants, and even those of other sects.
Having always recollected him, meditated upon him, and paid homage to him, he was worshipped by all the śrāvaka bhikṣus who were arhats and practitioners of the holy life.
Likewise, all the great beings and bodhisattvas,
always maintaining the recollection of his virtues, should praise and pay homage to him.
Likewise, having heard of and seen those qualities by means of the Pratyekabuddhas, they shall always rejoice, bow down, and offer praise.
Thus, all the lords of sages and the perfectly awakened ones always praise and rejoice in the greatness of that merit and virtue.
Thus he is the Lord of all worlds, the sovereign lord of all phenomena,
the creator of the manifold universe, the sustainer of the world, and the supreme ruler of the triple realm.
Born from the essence of the Great Buddha, a sun of the qualities of the True Dharma,
the sovereign lord of the entire Saṅgha, the Bodhisattva, the master of the world.
Thus it was proclaimed of old by all the Greatly Empowered Ones, the Perfectly Awakened Ones, the All-Seeing Lords of Munis— indeed, as I have heard it.
Thus, at the beginning, when even the five elements had not yet arisen, there arose the Great Void; then the primordial Buddha, stainless and like a light that has not emerged [from a source],
arose as the universal form, the great embodiment consisting of the portions of the three qualities.
That self-existent one, the Great Buddha, the Primordial Lord, the Great Sovereign,
himself entered the meditative absorption named "The Creation of the World."
Then, born from his own self, there appeared a divine form, bearing auspicious portions,
possessing a gracious appearance, with pure limbs, and adorned with excellent marks.
He who shines with the splendor of merit and beauty, the sovereign lord of all worlds,
himself performed the meditative absorption named "Arising of the World."
Then, from the eyes of that Ādinātha, the moon and the sun were born; and from his forehead, Maheśvara was born.
From his two shoulders was born the gentle, four-faced Brahmā;
and from his heart arose Nārāyaṇa, exceedingly beautiful.
From both rows of teeth Sarasvatī was produced;
from your mouth Vāyu was born, and from your feet the Earth was born.
Varuṇa was born from the belly, and Vahni from the circle of the navel;
Lakṣmī arose from the left knee, and Śrīda from the right knee.
In this way, other gods as well, even the lords of all worlds,
were born from the body of that Great-Souled One for the illumination of the world.
When these [beings] became lords of the world from the body of that Lord of the World,
they all stood nearby, gazing with serene faces.
Then the god Maheśvara, having prostrated before that creator, the teacher of the world, and gazing at him with palms joined in reverence, made this request with great devotion.
O Blessed One, since we have all been created by you,
please grant a formal prophecy for us all according to the proper rite for that purpose.
When Maheśvara had thus made his request,
the omniscient Lord of the World (Lokeśvara), having gazed upon them all, commanded them in this way.
O Maheśvara, you will become the lord of the formless realm;
a protector, a sovereign of yoga, a teacher, and a guide to the bliss of liberation from saṃsāra.
When the Kali age has fully arisen and the realm of sentient beings has become defiled,
you will then become the creator, the sustainer, and the destroyer.
All sentient beings are of evil conduct, devoted to the practices of Māra and infatuated with him; they have fallen into false teachings, are wicked, and revile the virtues of the True Dharma.

When the Kali age arrives, those who have abandoned the limbs of the bodhisattva practice, who cultivate qualities of darkness, and who are passionately attached to the teachings of non-Buddhist outsiders will come into being.
At that time, all ordinary beings— those possessed of delusion, envy, pride, and arrogance—
all of them will go for refuge and shall worship [him] with constant reverence.
They say that space is the *liṅga* and the earth is its pedestal;
it is called the *liṅga* because it is the abode (*ālaya*) of all beings and because [all things] dissolve (*līyanāt*) into it.
Thus, at that time, all people, speaking out of negligence and being utterly deluded, will reject all the gods and act accordingly.
Having observed them all and awakened them with diligent effort,
and having established them on the path to liberation, propagate the Śaiva vow.
Having acted thus and attained the station of Maheśāna,
you shall become the Lord Maheśvara, the sovereign and protector of the three worlds in the Kali age.
Having heard this command thus given, that Maheśvara,
having rejoiced with the words "So be it," took up his residence right there.
Then that teacher, the omniscient Lord of the World, the son of the Victor,
having addressed Brahmā and looking upon him, spoke as follows.
O Brahman, you are the sustainer of the four Vedas and the six auxiliary sciences;
the creator of the world, the teacher of the universe, and one who dwells in the four divine abodes.
He will be one whose conduct is peaceful and disciplined, a leader in the dharma of the sattvic nature, a learned master of the yoga of ultimate reality, and a bearer of auspicious purposes.
When the Kali age has arisen, your conduct will perish;
when the world is overwhelmed by the dharma of the Mlecchas, the practice of the virtuous will be abandoned.
Even then, you shall diligently awaken beings through various forms.
Having established them on the path of Dharma, lead them to perfect nirvana.
Thus, O Brahmā, having beheld all sentient beings and awakening them,
establish them on the path to enlightenment and protect the world for its welfare.
By acting thus, you will cross over the great ocean of existence and its afflictions;
having attained Arhatship and perfect enlightenment, you too shall become a fully awakened Buddha.
Having heard what was thus commanded by him and being awakened,
Brahmā, having assented with "So be it," rejoiced, being thoroughly gratified.
Then that Great Being, Lokeśvara, the very embodiment of the Victor,
gazed upon Nārāyaṇa and, having addressed him, commanded thus:
O Viṣṇu, you are the lord of the realm of desire, the sovereign of all worlds, the master,
the ruler of the quality of passion, the teacher who bears the welfare of all sentient beings.
Possessing great supernormal knowledge, a great hero, the crusher of all that is wicked,
the provider of the happiness of saṃsāra, and one who is skilled in the illusory nature of phenomena.
In this age of strife, awaken beings who are agitated by afflictions through various means;
even by frightening them, you must diligently establish them all in the Dharma.
Having acted thus, the Great Being, endowed with great merit and virtue,
became the sovereign King Viśvambhara, the protector and lord of fortune, possessed of great supernatural power.

Having brought happiness to all sentient beings and having completely conquered all who are malevolent, you, whose self is restrained by conventional morality, will ultimately attain the state of nirvana.
Having heard what was thus commanded by him, Viṣṇu was awakened; having replied "So be it," he was gratified and rejoiced.
Then that Great Being, Lokeśvara, born from a portion of the Victor,
looked upon Sarasvatī and, having addressed her, commanded thus:
Sarasvatī is the Great Goddess, the source of all knowledge and virtues;
she is the wielder of great illusion, the knower of all scriptures, and the speaker of sublime words.
"You shall become Vāgīśvarī, the gatherer of the qualities of the True Dharma, the protector of perfect enlightenment, and the bestower of supernatural powers and accomplishments."
Having diligently awakened all beings— even those who are foolish or of evil conduct— join them to the auspicious Dharma and protect them.
Those wise ones who, having gone for refuge, should honor [him] with devoted minds, would become possessors of great superknowledges and abodes of glorious qualities.
Having thus acted for the benefit of sentient beings, endowed with great merit and virtue,
you will eventually attain awakening and reach the state of a Victor.
Having heard this command of his, Sarasvatī,
having greeted him with "So be it," withdrew to a secluded spot there.
Then that Great Being, Lokeśvara, the son of the Conqueror,
having gazed upon Virocana and addressed him, spoke thus:
O Sun, you are the lord of the planets who produces great blazing light;
as the maker of day, you shall become the ender of the darkness of the world.
Having illuminated the world of beings, making it manifest and purifying it,
and having established them in the auspicious Dharma, protect [them] always as you wander.
Then that Great Being, the Lord of the World and Master of the Universe,
having looked at the moon and addressed him, gave this command:
You shall become the Moon, possessing great luster, with cool rays, the source of nectar, the lord of the stars,
who removes the fever of affliction from the world.
Illuminating the world of living beings and raining down the nectar of immortality,
I cause the essence and potency of medicinal herbs, rice, and crops to increase.
Having endowed all beings with the happiness of Prahlāda, awakening them at night and setting them upon the auspicious Dharma, protect them.
Then, having observed Vāyu, that omniscient Lord of the World addressed them all and instructed him in this manner right before them.
May you all, the winds— the life-breaths of the world that bring happiness—
become the instigators of joy and enthusiasm for all dharmas.
Always moving about, carrying the pleasant fragrance of virtue,
and having inspired the world toward the Dharma, may you protect it until the end of existence.
Then, having gazed upon the great goddess Pṛthvī, the All-Seeing Son of the Jina, the Lord of the World, addressed her and commanded as follows:
O Earth, you are the sustainer of the world and the refuge of all people;
as Vasundharā, the supporter of the world, you shall become the Mother of the Universe.
Having given all elements, excellent jewels, rice, crops, and great medicinal herbs,
and having established them in the True Dharma, protect the world forever.
Then that Lord of the World, the embodiment of the Jina, beholding Varuṇa,
addressed him in his presence and prophesied, giving this command:
O Varuṇa, you shall become the lord of the waters, the source of the nectar of immortality for all sentient beings,
and the sovereign of all jewel-mines as a king of the nāgas.
Having nourished and awakened [beings] by the constant bestowal of the nectar of immortality,
and having given them jewels, cause the world to always practice the true Dharma.
Then, having beheld the fire, the radiant Citrabhānu,
the Teacher and Lord of all worlds addressed him and commanded thus:
O Vahni, you have become the mouth of all the gods and the consumer of the sacrificial oblation;
you are the ripener of all things, the burner, and indeed the purifier.
Therefore, with every effort, gladdening all the worlds and always bestowing happiness upon them, protect the world for its welfare.
Then that wise Lord of the World, having summoned the great goddess Lakṣmī before him and gazed upon her, commanded her thus:
O Lakṣmī, you shall become the illustrious Great Goddess Māheśvarī, the Earth,
the bestower of all prosperity and the joy of exertion.
Having bestowed even the great riches and pleasures of the world, including its elements, substances, and boundaries, and having established them in the Dharma, protect the world forever.
Then, having beheld Śrīda, that Lord of the World and Master of the Universe addressed him from his presence and, having explained [the matter], gave this divine command:
O Kubera, you shall be highly fortunate, the sovereign lord of all wealth,
the repository of prosperity, abundance, and excellent virtues, and the king of kings.
Having bestowed the perfections of glorious virtues, having granted them, and awakening them,
establish them on the path to enlightenment and protect the world forever.
Thus did that Lord of the Three Worlds, Lokeśvara, the Son of the Victor,
address all those gods who were his own offspring and issue this command.
All of you, great beings who practice the vow of perfect enlightenment,
act always for the welfare of all sentient beings and proceed ever toward what is auspicious.
Having thus performed this great merit, endowed with glory and prosperity,
you shall in the end attain perfect awakening and reach the state of a fully enlightened Buddha.
Having heard this command thus issued, all those gods were awakened; rejoicing, they promised, "So be it."
Thus all those gods, having received his instruction and having resolved upon the conduct of awakening, proceeded for the welfare of the world.
Precisely because of his instruction, even the lords of all worlds,
having taken up the vow of the conduct of awakening, have proceeded for the welfare of the world.
Thus is he the teacher of the three worlds, the Lord of the World, the Son of the Victor,
a Bodhisattva possessing great supernormal knowledges, and the sovereign lord of all the worlds.
All those who, with faith, have gone for refuge to that Lord of the Three Worlds,
being pure in soul, never go to an evil rebirth.
Always born into happy realms, endowed with the glory and happiness of the true Dharma,
and free from afflictions, may they attain enlightenment and reach the state of a perfect Buddha.
All the Sugatas have gone for refuge through faith in him;
having cultivated meditative recollection and teaching it, they proceed for the welfare of the world.
By the power of this merit, having become free from afflictions and pure in intention,
they conquered the hosts of Māra, attained enlightenment, and reached perfect nirvāṇa.
The perfectly awakened ones of the past, those of the present, and those of the future—
all of them have gone for refuge with faith to the Teacher of the World.
Having meditated and established mindfulness, while acting for the welfare of the world,
and having maintained the vow of the conduct of awakening, one brings about the benefit of all beings.
Having gradually fulfilled the equipment for enlightenment according to the prescribed method,
and having conquered all the hosts of Māra, they attained enlightenment and became Victors.
There have been and there will be Dharma-kings, lords of sages,
Arhats, Sugatas, Protectors, omniscient ones, and leaders of the three worlds.
Thus is that Lord of the Three Worlds, the powerful Lokeśvara,
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, the sovereign lord of all the worlds.
Practicing the vow of the conduct of awakening for the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings,
he himself beholds, illuminates, and delivers all sentient beings.
Having established them on the path to enlightenment and caused them to practice the auspicious Dharma,
he awakens those who are well-pleased and sends them to Sukhāvatī.
Thus, that Lord of the World, the Sovereign of the World, the Son of the Victor,
is a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who upholds the welfare and purpose of all phenomena.
There is no one equal to him in terms of merit and the qualities of the true Dharma;
how could there be anyone superior to him, the Lord of the World and Master of the Universe?
Thus have all the Sugatas, the perfectly awakened ones who see all things, taught the greatness of the qualities of Lokeśvara; this I have heard.
I previously heard from Minīndra that such was the manifestation of the merit and qualities of the wise Lokeśvara.
Therefore, Lokeśvaravara, the lord of the entire assembly and the teacher of the world,
who possesses the qualities of the true Dharma, should be served with diligent effort by those who desire the virtues of the true Dharma.
For those who, having gone to him for refuge, honor him with faith and joy,
never go to an evil rebirth anywhere at any time.
Always born into fortunate rebirths, partaking in the joy of the glory of the Dharma,
they enjoy auspicious enthusiasm and in the end go to Sukhāvatī.
Having heard these instructions thus given by the Protector, the Lion of the Śākyas, all the people in the assembly rejoiced, being awakened to understanding.
Thus ends the section on the manifestation of the deities beginning with the illustrious Maheśvara.
5. The Chapter on Awakening All Beings in Every Way and Introducing Them to the Practice of Bodhicitta.
Then Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, the son of the Sugata, having bowed with palms joined to the Blessed One, spoke as follows:
O Blessed One, when will that Mahāsattva, the Lord of the World and Master of the Universe, arrive here? I wish to behold that Lord.
Having heard what was thus spoken, the Blessed One, that lord of sages,
looked toward the great being Viṣkambhin and commanded him as follows.
That Great Being Viṣkambhin would not come here at this time;
rather, he goes elsewhere to rescue sentient beings from hell.
Going everywhere himself and beholding all those beings who have resorted to the hells, he delivers them all and sends them to Sukhāvatī.
Thus, seeing beings for himself every day,
he constantly delivers incalculable numbers of them and sends them to Sukhāvatī.
Acting thus, that Lord of the World, practicing the vow of the conduct of awakening,
shines forth, enriched by the glory of countless jewels of merit and other such excellences.
His merit is incalculable, immeasurable, and most excellent;
it cannot be measured even by all the lords of sages.
Thus was it previously proclaimed by all the Sugatas; this I have heard, and now I shall proclaim it here—listen to me with respect.
Just as in the past there was a Teacher named Śikhin,
a Tathāgata, omniscient, an Arhat, possessed of great super-knowledge, a King of Dharma, and Lord of Sages.
The sovereign lord of all vidyās, the perfectly awakened one, the Sugata, the Victor;
the conqueror of Māra, the lord of all worlds, the guide of the triple realm.
At that time, I was a householder bodhisattva named Dānaśūra,
a steadfast man who delighted always in giving and bore the welfare of all sentient beings as his purpose.
Always approaching that Lord of Sages, the Teacher of the World, he constantly worshipped him with reverence and faith.
At that time, I heard it explained by that Lord of Sages:
the skill in generating the practice of the True Dharma of Lokeśvara.
Having heard what was thus proclaimed by that Lord of Sages,
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Viṣkambhin spoke as follows.
"Blessed One, what kind of skillfulness regarding the accomplishment of the true Dharma have you heard from that great-souled Lokeśvara?"
O Blessed One, having explained that, awaken us all;
having heard it, may all these people become devoted to its virtues.
Having heard this prayer thus offered by him, the Blessed One, the Victor,
looked upon all those seated in the assembly and gave this instruction:
When that Blessed One, the Teacher, the Tathāgata Śikhin, the Victor,
was seated together with his Saṅgha in the midst of the assembly of all the worlds.

In order to fully teach the True Dharma— which is virtuous in the beginning, middle, and end, and which accomplishes the qualities of perfect enlightenment— I shall begin for the welfare of the world.
Then, from the opening of his mouth, various-colored divine rays issued forth, illuminating the entire world and streaming everywhere.
Having performed auspicious deeds everywhere throughout all the worlds on every side,
that radiance returned and arrived once more at that hermitage.
Having circumambulated three times that Śikhin, the possessor of great supernormal knowledge, the King of Dharma, the Lord of Sages, he entered into the fire from his mouth.
Having seen that true radiance of merit, Lokeśvara was struck with wonder;
having bowed to the Jina Amitābha, he asked this with great reverence:
"Blessed One, whose auspicious splendor of merit has arrived here? O Teacher, may you kindly instruct us and awaken our understanding."
Having heard what was thus spoken, the Blessed One Amitaprabha looked toward the Great Being Lokeśvara and commanded him as follows.
Noble son, there was a perfectly awakened one named Śikhin, an Arhat, Lord of Sages, the Omniscient One, Teacher of the Three Worlds, King of Dharma, and Tathāgata.
He resided together with the Saṅgha in the Jeta Grove monastery.
Seated in the midst of the assembly of all worlds, illuminating [them],
he now begins to fully teach the true Dharma.
This beautiful radiance of his has issued forth from the gateway of his mouth;
thus it proceeds, illuminating all the worlds.
Having arrived here as well, illuminating and spreading abroad,
it now enters the mouth of that Sage after having undergone transformation.
Having been thus instructed by the Lord of Sages, the Lord of the World was gratified;
he bowed down to that Lord of Sages, Amitābha, and spoke as follows.
"O Blessed One, I wish to see that King of Dharma right now;
I shall go there, so it behooves you to grant me permission."
Having heard this prayer made by Lokeśa,
Amitābha, the Lord of Sages, spoke thus to that Lokeśa:
"Noble son, if you wish to see that Lord of Sages, go; by my word as well, you ought to touch upon skillful means."
Having approached the lotus and beheld its assembly hall,
and having taken refuge in the True Dharma and heard it, one should depart with joy.
Having heard these instructions from the Lord of Sages, Lokeśvara, with joy and palms joined in reverence, bowed to the Jina and then proceeded on his way while conversing with him.
Then, as he set out for Sukhāvatī, illuminating the way,
the entire earth, together with its oceans and its depths, trembled.
From the sky, there rained down great lotuses made of gold and jewels;
free from any ill omen, they fell everywhere with auspicious intensity.
Then, in the great garden of that hermitage, wish-fulfilling trees (kalpavṛkṣas) arose,
hung with divine garments, gold, and other jewels and ornaments.
There were various flowering trees adorned with fragrant blossoms,
and many fruit-bearing trees bent low under the weight of fruits of divine flavor.
Delightful lakes, filled with water endowed with the eight qualities and strewn with various flowers, appeared.
Various substances of diverse flower-like colors,
as well as metals such as gold, precious gems, garments, and ornaments.
Then, in that hermitage, there rained down various kinds of grain and rice, as well as foods endowed with the excellent taste and flavor of gold.
And there, in the hermitage of the Jina, the seven precious gems appeared;
and then the entire ground, being made of gold, shone forth with radiance.
Then Lokeśvara, moving forward, took up a thousand-petaled golden lotus, blazing and composed of the seven precious gems.
Thus, manifesting there the signs of auspiciousness,
he illuminated the world of beings and surveyed it on all sides.
Having diligently uplifted all sentient beings who are suffering and having established them on the path to enlightenment, he sends them forth to Sukhāvatī.
Emitting rays of nectar and illuminating everything all around,
he approached the dwelling of the perfectly awakened Śikhin.
Having observed those auspicious omens, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ratnapāṇi, seated in that assembly, gazed intently.
Filled with wonder, he rose up suddenly; emaciated, he approached him, wearing his upper garment and resting upon the ground on his knees.
Having joyfully bowed with palms joined in reverence to the Blessed One, the Lord of Sages, the Fully Awakened Śikhin, he questioned him thus with great respect.
"Bhagavān, whose radiant splendor has come here? Great and auspicious omens are seen arising."
O Blessed One, having instructed all these members of this assembly,
you ought to awaken them, whose inner minds are agitated with wonder.
Having heard this prayer made by him, the Tathāgata Śikhin,
looking upon that Mahāsattva Ratnapāṇi, gave this instruction:
O Great Being Ratnapāṇi, great and auspicious omens are now seen here on every side.
I shall fully explain the cause of that; listen to this with respect.
All of you, being gracious, understand it and rejoice.
He who is the glorious Lord of the World, the Bodhisattva, the Son of the Conqueror;
the sovereign of the entire Saṅgha, the Teacher, the lord of the masters of all worlds;
he who acts as Samantabhadra—that is the noble Avalokiteśvara.
Beholding sentient beings, he sets forth for Sukhāvatī in order to deliver them.
Emitting rays of merit, illuminating all directions,
purifying the world of the three realms, and bringing auspiciousness everywhere;
Beholding even those evildoers of wicked conduct who are submerged everywhere, even in the hells, [the Lord] lifts them up from all sides.
Having awakened them with great effort and made them yearn for the true Dharma,
she has now come here to behold me;
it is this very Suprabhā, radiant with splendor, who has arrived.
Such omens have arisen on all sides;
this is surely for the sake of the welfare of that Lokeśvara who has arrived.
Having heard these instructions from the Lord of Sages, Ratnapāṇi,
beholding the Fully Awakened One and that assembly, spoke as follows:
O Blessed One, that Mahāsattva, the Lord of the World, the Master of the Universe—why does he not come? When will I see that Lord? I desire to behold him.
Having heard what was thus spoken by him, the Blessed One, the Victorious One Śikhin, looked toward Ratnapāṇi and the assembly, and gave this instruction:
That Mahāsattva, the Lord of the World (Lokeśvara), having rescued all sentient beings and sent them to Sukhāvatī, might come here, deeply distressed.
First, let that ocean of compassion come here to see me;
then, after that, worship that Lord of the Three Worlds with great devotion.
Having heard these instructions from the Lord of Sages, that bearer of jewels stood with joy alongside all those in the assembly, eager for the vision of him.
Then that Lord of the Three Worlds, the Sovereign of the World, illuminating all,
saw the Sugata from afar and entered the monastery.
Beholding that Lord of the World, the son of the Sugata, who had arrived there,
all the people seated in the assembly rose and bowed down to him.
Seeing him arrive, Ratnapāṇi rose up suddenly;
approaching with palms joined in reverence, he paid homage at his lotus feet.
Thus being honored by all those people and illuminating everything,
he beheld Śikhin before him and approached him.
Seeing that he had arrived, the Blessed One Śikhin joyfully asked, "Welcome to you, O Great Being; are you well?"
Having heard these instructions from the Lord of Sages, that son of the Sugata attended upon him, saying,
"O Teacher, may I always be skillful."
There, that Lord of the Three Worlds, having paid homage to the lord of sages Śikhin and having presented that great lotus, spoke as follows.
O Blessed One, this lotus has been sent by the Teacher Amitābha;
he also inquires after your welfare in every respect from all sides.
Having heard what was thus spoken, the blessed Lord Śikhin joyfully took that great lotus, placed it upon his left side, and spoke as follows.
"Is there skill in all things here, or is there skill in only some? Having been asked this by the Lords of Sages, he replied as follows:
"Noble son, how many beings have been rescued by you from their reliance on the hells, established in auspicious states, and sent to Sukhāvatī?"
When the Lord of Sages had thus questioned him, Lokeśvara looked at the Fully Awakened One and, surveying the assembly as well, spoke as follows.
"Blessed One, there were many incalculable beings dwelling in the hells;
having observed them all with diligence, I have delivered them."
For example, those who are greatly wicked and experience the fruits of their karma in the Avīci hell, as well as in the Raurava, Kālasūtra, Hahava, and Tapana hells.
Those sinners who are in the Tāpana and Agniṣṭhāta hells, as well as those in the Śālmalika,
Saṃghāta, Andhatāmisra, Śītodaka, and Asipatraka hells;
In this way, throughout all the other hells as well,
they remain experiencing suffering, partaking of the fruits of their own past actions.
Scorched by the fire of intense suffering, deluded and deprived of their senses—
all of them have been rescued by me and sent to Sukhāvatī.
There are spirits, ghosts, and piśācas, tormented by the fires of hunger and thirst;
there are wicked beings such as the sūcimukhas and others, who feed upon excrement, urine, and impurities.
Even those beasts that are wicked, even those birds that are difficult to approach,
and even the worms, insects, and so forth, are all experiencers of the fruits of their own karma.
Having beheld them all, I have liberated them from their own karma;
having uplifted them with great effort, I have sent them forth to Sukhāvatī.
In the same way, other beings as well— those mortals, Daityas, and even Asuras who delight in unrighteousness, who are wicked and fallen— are destined for hell.
Having beheld them all and awakened them through diligent effort, I established them in the True Dharma and dispatched them to the abode of the Victors.
Thus, having constantly observed that all living beings were afflicted by evil deeds,
seated in every hell, and tormented by the fires of intense suffering;
Day after day, having diligently extracted [beings] even in incalculable numbers,
having awakened them, established them in virtue, and caused them to practice the excellent vows,
and having thus directed them onto the path to enlightenment, they are sent forth to the abode of the Victors.
"Whatever has been vowed by me must indeed be carried out accordingly";
having constantly reflected thus, sentient beings were encouraged toward the Dharma.
As long as there remain all living beings who have not yet attained a share in enlightenment, may I not attain perfect awakening for the welfare of the world.
Thus is my firm vow: until it is fully accomplished, I shall diligently observe all sentient beings and lift them up with effort.
Having awakened them and established them in the four divine abodes,
and having set them upon the path to enlightenment, I would send them to Sukhāvatī.
Thus, O Blessed One, may I practice the conduct of awakening;
having brought about the welfare of all sentient beings, may I wander even throughout the three realms.
Thus, having made the world eternally a festival of auspicious happiness, I move about in this manner; thus shall I always conduct myself within existence.
Having spoken thus, that Great Being, Lokeśvara, the son of the Victor,
bowed once more to Śikhin and requested his permission.
O Blessed One, I wish to go elsewhere to deliver sentient beings;
therefore, may you be gracious for the welfare of the world and grant me your permission.
Having heard what was thus spoken, the Blessed One Śikhin, filled with joy,
looked upon that Lokeśvara, who possesses great supernormal knowledge, and spoke as follows.
May your task, the accomplishment of perfect awakening, be successful, O Great Being!
Go forth and bring benefit to the world; may you always move through it in happiness.
Having been thus instructed by the Lord of Sages, Lokeśvara, the sovereign of the world,
bowed down to that Dharmarāja Śikhin and then proceeded from there.
Then, having set out, blazing like a mass of fire,
he vanished into the sky and departed elsewhere, illuminating the earth.
Seeing him thus gone into the sky, Ratnapāṇi was filled with wonder;
looking toward the Blessed One Śikhin, he spoke as follows.
O Blessed One, how great is the accumulation of merit possessed by this king, the lord of the three worlds? Please instruct us on that.
Having heard this prayer offered by him, the Blessed One Śikhin,
holding a jewel in his hand, looked at him, addressed him, and commanded as follows:
Listen, noble son, and I shall proclaim the mass of merit of this Lokeśvara, the Lord of the World, for the sake of the welfare of sentient beings.
For example, there are certain great beings who, remaining present, serve all embodied beings at all times with every form of honor.
"All the merits belonging to them, however many there may be, are equal to a single hair-tip of the World-Lord, the True Guru"— thus all the Victors have proclaimed.
It is as if clouds were to rain constantly over the four continents;
I am able to count every single drop of all that water.
But no one at all is able to measure the extent of the mass of merit belonging to this Bodhisattva Lokeśvara, the possessor of true power.
I am certainly able to count every single drop of water in all the oceans and in all bodies of water.
But I am truly unable to calculate the number of the accumulations of merit of this Lord of the World, who practices the vow of perfect enlightenment.
Indeed, it is said that the number of all living beings dwelling in the four continents can be measured by the count of each individual hair on their bodies.
But it is not possible for me to measure the merit of the accumulations for enlightenment belonging to this Lord of the World, who is an ocean of the true Dharma and sublime qualities.
Having fashioned stūpas made of gold and jewels, as numerous as atoms of dust, and having worshipped them at all times, one should devote oneself [to practice] while remaining present.
Likewise, having established images of the Perfectly Awakened One, equal in number to atoms of dust,
made of gold and jewels, all the worlds [would celebrate] with great festivals.
May they always worship with joy through the limbs of the seven-jeweled offering;
I am certainly able to calculate the measure of this merit.
I am utterly unable in any way to calculate the measure or the number of the merits of this Lord of the World, who dwells in the four sublime abodes.
Indeed, I am able to calculate the exact number of leaves upon all trees, even those great trees that grow in the four continents.
I am never able to calculate the measure of the merit of this Lord of the World, who bestows the welfare of all sentient beings.
All men and women, mortals dwelling in the four continents,
having established them in the fruit of stream-entry, should cause them to observe the excellent restraint.
Indeed, I am able to calculate the measure of their merit;
however, I would not be able to measure the merit of the Lords of the World.
Having diligently awakened all these men as well,
and having made them once-returners, they should always cause them to practice what is auspicious.
Indeed, it is possible to measure even these merits;
however, the merits of Lokeśa can never be measured anywhere.
And likewise, having awakened all human beings and rejoicing with them,
they should establish them in the fruit of a non-returner (anāgāmiphala) and cause them to practice in the excellent restraint.
Indeed, it is possible to measure even these merits;
however, it is never possible to measure the merit of this Lord of the World.
In the same way, having diligently awakened all these mortals and established them in the state of an Arhat, they would cause them to dwell in perfect nirvāṇa.
I am able to measure even these merits,
but not those of this Lord of the World, even by the Sugatas themselves.
Likewise, having awakened all these people even to the enlightenment of a Pratyekabuddha and having enjoined them to it, they would cause them to dwell in perfect nirvana.
I am able to measure even these merits,
but not those of this Lord of the World, even by all the lords of sages combined.
Of all these merits,
the merit of this Lord of the World is the most excellent, great, vast, immeasurable, and supreme.
How could that merit be measured here by me alone?
Indeed, it can never be measured even by all the Lords of Sages.
Thus is he, the Lord of the World, the Great Being, the Bodhisattva, the Son of the Conqueror, endowed with the magnificent splendor of a vast accumulation of merit.
Indeed, there is no other great being even within the three realms who possesses such an abundance of the glory of the noble qualities of the equipment of merit.
Having thus heard of that great merit, may you be filled with joy; having gone for refuge to that Lord, worship him always throughout existence.
Those who, having meditated upon the name of that Lord of the Three Worlds, the Sovereign of the World, the Master of the Universe, utter it and remember it, always worship him.
Freed from the afflictions of existence, with the three spheres completely purified,
and endowed with the virtues of the glory of the Dharma, they proceeded to Sukhāvatī.
Having gone there with joy for refuge to the Lord Amitābha,
those seekers of awakening, having tasted the nectar of the true Dharma, shall rejoice.
They shall never again be afflicted by the defilements of worldly existence;
they shall not experience the great suffering of dwelling in a womb, nor shall they undergo rebirth.
Having meditated constantly upon that supreme lord of sages, they shall be born within a lotus made of jewels in that very Sukhāvatī and remain there forever.
They shall remain there in Sukhāvatī, endowed with happiness,
for as long as the vow of this Teacher of the World has not been fully accomplished.
Having gradually fulfilled the equipment for enlightenment for the welfare of the world,
and having attained the threefold awakening, may they reach the state of a perfectly enlightened Buddha.
Thus have I heard all that was taught by the Sugatas;
may those who desire awakening devote themselves to this Lord of the World.
Having heard this instruction from the Lord of Sages, Ratnapāṇi looked toward the Blessed One, Śikhin, and spoke as follows.
Blessed One, this vow of his is so very firm and so exceedingly great;
in how much time, indeed, will it be fully accomplished?
How is it that by means of that single self, all those dwelling in the three realms were established on the path to enlightenment and dispatched to Sukhāvatī?
How can this Great Being, alone, awaken all those beings who lack resolute conviction and apply them all to the path to enlightenment?
Sentient beings born within the six realms of existence follow various courses of karma;
how can one person alone awaken and bring all of them to maturity?
Having heard what was thus spoken by him, the Blessed One, the Victorious One Śikhin,
looked toward the Great Being Ratnapāṇi and spoke as follows.
Though he is but one great being, possessing great supernormal knowledge and born from a portion of the Victor,
he taught the true Dharma to sentient beings in various forms.
Awakening all living beings and having given them whatever wealth they desire,
he establishes them on the path to enlightenment and sends them to the abode of the Victors.
Appearing in the form of a wise teacher to those who are to be awakened, he enjoins them to the Buddha-dharma,
establishes them on the path to enlightenment, and sends them to Sukhāvatī.
To those who desire the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha, he appears in the form of a pratyekabuddha,
establishes them on the path to awakening, and sends them to perfect nirvāṇa.
Awakening those who are deeply attached to the qualities of an Arhat by appearing in the form of an Arhat,
he establishes them in the qualities of an Arhat and sends them to Sukhāvatī.
Seeking the conduct of awakening, they awaken [beings] in the form of bodhisattvas;
establishing them in the vow of the conduct of awakening, they cause them to practice for the welfare of the world.
Likewise, appearing in the form of a lay follower, he awakens those who are lay followers.
Having established them on the path to enlightenment, he practices excellent self-restraint.
And thus, manifesting in the form of Śiva and awakening all the followers of Śiva,
he establishes them on the path to enlightenment and leads them for the welfare of the world.
Thus, manifesting in the form of Viṣṇu, he awakens all the Vaiṣṇavas;
having established them on the path to enlightenment, he acts for the welfare of the world.
And likewise, awakening all the Brahmins by means of the form of Brahmā,
and having established them on the path to enlightenment, they act for the welfare of the world.
In the same way, awakening even all those who possess the forms of Indra and non-Indra,
he establishes them on the path to enlightenment and causes them to act for the welfare of the world.
Likewise, awakening those to be trained by the Sun through the form of the Sun,
he establishes them on the path to enlightenment and causes them to act for the welfare of the world.
Likewise, by assuming the form of the moon, he awakens those who are to be disciplined by the moon;
having established them on the path to enlightenment, he causes them to act for the welfare of the world.
And so, by appearing in the form of fire to those who are to be disciplined by fire,
he establishes them on the path to enlightenment and causes them to act for the welfare of the world.
And likewise, he awakened those to be trained by Yama by appearing in the form of Yama; similarly, he awakened those to be trained by Varuṇa by appearing in the form of Varuṇa.
And likewise, he awakened those to be disciplined by means of wind through the form of wind,
and he awakened even those to be disciplined by the Rākṣasa through the form of a Rākṣasa.
Awakening those to be trained by a yakṣa through the form of a yakṣa,
and awakening those to be trained by a nāga through the form of a nāga.
Likewise, by means of the form of Bhūteśa, he [tames] those to be converted who are devoted to spirits;
and likewise, by means of the form of Gaṇeśa, he [tames] those to be converted who are devoted to the Lord of the Gaṇas.
Likewise, he appears in the form of a gandharva for those who practice the dharma of the gandharvas;
likewise, he appears in the form of a kinnara for those to be disciplined by a kinnara.
In the form of a Vidyādhara, he awakens the Vidyādharas;
likewise, in the form of Bhairava, he awakens those who are to be disciplined by Bhairava.
Likewise, he awakened those to be disciplined as youths by appearing in the form of Skanda.
Awakening those to be trained through the form of Mahākāla,
awakening those to be trained through the form of Mahākāla.
Awakening those to be trained by means of the forms of the Mothers,
and establishing them on the path to enlightenment, he causes them to act for the welfare of the world.
Thus, by means of whatever vehicle he awakens whichever sentient beings are to be trained,
he applies himself in that very form for the welfare of the world.
Thus, that sage enlightened those to be guided by means of the form of a sage, and he enlightened the practitioners of yoga by means of the form of a yogin.

And so, he awakened those to be trained by an ascetic through the form of an ascetic, and likewise awakened those to be trained by an ascetic through penance through the form of one practicing penance.
Likewise, he awakens the heretics by appearing in the form of a heretic;
and similarly, he awakens those who are to be disciplined by a king by appearing in the form of a king.
Awakening those to be trained who are of the Vaiśya class by appearing in the form of a Vaiśya,
and awakening those to be trained who are of the Śūdra class by appearing in the form of a Śūdra.
Awakening those to be disciplined by the householder through that very form,
he likewise awakened those to be disciplined by a minister through the form of a minister.
Likewise, he awakened those to be disciplined by him in the form of a minister;
and similarly, he awakened some of those to be disciplined as warriors in the form of a warrior.
And thus, some he [approached] in the form of a servant, some in the form of a slave,
some in the form of a caravan leader, and some in the form of a fisherman.
And likewise, he appeared to some in the form of a physician, to some in the form of a merchant,
to some in the form of a father, and to some in the form of a mother.
And likewise, some he [perceived] in the form of brothers, some in the form of wives,
some in the form of sisters, and some in the form of sons.
Some appear in the form of daughters, some in the form of grandsons;
likewise, they appear as paternal grandfathers and so forth, as kinsmen, and even as friends.
Awakening some by means of the forms of kinsmen, friends, and companions, and diligently terrifying others by means of the form of an enemy;
To some he appears in the form of a caṇḍāla, and to others in the form of a thief;
having thus impelled them toward the True Dharma, he acts for the welfare of the world.
Thus, even while terrifying them with the forms of lions and other creatures,
he [terrified] beasts and birds, as well as living beings such as worms and insects.
Having terrified them by means of his form and having awakened them with great effort,
he establishes them on the path to enlightenment and causes the world to practice what is auspicious.
Thus this Great Being, the Lord of the World and Master of the Universe,
awakens the minds of all sentient beings through various forms.
Even while striking fear [into the wicked], you diligently urge [beings] toward the true Dharma.
Thus that Lord of the Three Worlds, the Bodhisattva, the Son of the Victor,
having delivered all sentient beings, sends them to Sukhāvatī.
Having done this, that Lord of the World, the sovereign lord of all the lords of the world,
[acted] toward those wandering in the existence of the six realms of rebirth, even the wicked and the deluded.
Possessing the glory of the true Dharma, excellent virtues, and the abundance of great sovereignty.
There is no one equal to him, even in terms of merit, glory, or virtue; he is compassionate and moves with auspicious conduct throughout all the worlds of the three realms.
Thus, recognizing his great merit, those who desire perfect enlightenment go to him for refuge with faith; they honor him by recollecting and meditating upon him.
Those who, having gone to him for refuge, remember, meditate upon, and worship him—
all of them indeed become pure-souled, noble-minded, and possessed of auspicious faculties.
Bodhisattvas, the great beings, always practicing what is virtuous,
shall attain the state of nirvāṇa after accomplishing the threefold awakening.
Having heard these instructions from the Lord of Sages, Ratnapāṇi,
his heart overcome with great wonder, spoke as follows.
O Blessed One, I have attained supreme wonder that such a majesty of the qualities of the glory of the Dharma has never been seen anywhere, nor even heard of.
Such an accumulation of merit as this is never seen even among the Victors; indeed, it has never been heard by me at any time.
Having heard what was thus spoken by him, the Blessed One, the Victorious One Śikhin, looked toward the Mahāsattva Ratnapāṇi and commanded him as follows:
Possessing the most excellent portion of all forms, he is like a gem of universal form,
bearing the welfare and purpose of all like a great wish-fulfilling jewel.
Like the wish-fulfilling cow (kāmadhenu), he is a collection of prosperity to be enjoyed according to one's desires;
like the wish-granting tree (kalpavṛkṣa), he is the bestower of auspicious glory and abundant success.
Just as a broken jar fulfills the desires of all beings,
so too does that Lord of the World fulfill the desired aims of everyone.
The Bodhisattva is the sustainer of the world, the Lord of All, the Master of the World;
he is the sovereign of all phenomena, the Teacher, and the supreme lord of all the worlds.
What can be said of his majesty, who is filled with the virtues of the glory of awakening?
It cannot be fully described even by all the lords of sages.
Just as that Great Being awakens even those who are difficult to tame,
establishes them on the path to enlightenment, and causes them to act for the welfare of the world.
The cave of the Vajra-womb is renowned; it exists here in Jambudvīpa, where many thousands of the enemies of the gods once dwelt.
Having gone there, wandering in the form of a teacher among the gods,
he approached them as he beheld them, in order to fully teach the true Dharma.
Seeing that the teacher had arrived, all those asuras approached him suddenly with joy, bowed down, and spoke thus:
"Welcome to you; you have arrived at the right time," they said, having thus bowed down.
Welcome to you, O Samayasin; may you be well in every respect.
Having looked upon us with compassion, you should deign to teach us the Dharma.
Whatever you have instructed us, exactly as it was taught,
we shall respectfully hear, retain, and practice for the sake of achieving the pleasures of saṃsāra.
Thus all the Dānavas joyfully entreated their preceptor; having established him upon his seat in the assembly, they took their places to listen to the Dharma.
Seeing all those [asuras] seated together, that son of the Sugata taught the true Dharma, beginning with the Dharma for the Daityas.
Sirs, listen to the Dharma that is the means for achieving happiness in saṃsāra;
I shall speak here for the sake of your liberation from the suffering of saṃsāra.
O sirs, be here possessed of a mind of loving-kindness, a peaceful mind, and conquered senses; be compassionate toward sentient beings and practitioners of right conduct.
Therefore, with truthful conduct and pure intentions, having joyfully gone for refuge to the Triple Gem, observe the Poṣadha vow.
Having observed that king of vows which brings about auspiciousness within saṃsāra,
listen also to the sublime speech of the Kāraṇḍavyūha Sūtra.
Those who, having heard this well-spoken king of Mahāyāna sūtras,
go for refuge to the Triple Gem and practice the Poṣadha vow;
All their sins, even the five acts of immediate retribution,
will be completely and utterly destroyed throughout all of existence.
And those who, having heard it, recite it, will faithfully believe it with reverence,
will grasp it, write it down, and joyfully study it.
And those who shall cause it to be written, who shall recite it at all times,
who shall constantly reflect upon it, and who shall cultivate it with reverence;
They will teach the meaning in detail to others with reverence;
they will always and at all times honor them with offerings and faith.
They alone are happy and blessed, partaking in the joys of saṃsāra;
they shall never at any time experience the sufferings of the miserable realms.
Always born into noble states of existence, they enjoy the pleasures of saṃsāra;
possessing the splendor of excellent qualities and great success, they are endowed with great supernatural powers.
Having undertaken the vow of the conduct of awakening, they will strive for the benefit of themselves and others,
performing auspicious deeds everywhere and always remaining within cyclic existence.
In their final births, they will remember their past lives; with their intentions set upon awakening, they will take refuge in the Three Jewels and attain perfect nirvana.
When the time had come for those who desired liberation,
the twelve Sugatas, having looked upon them, approached and stood before them face-to-face.
Having perceived them standing nearby and touched them with the nectar-rays of their merit,
they look upon them, console them, and thus honor them with great respect.
"Do not fear, noble son; remain here. Enough with this lack of fortitude, for you have heard the Mahāyānasaṃghāṭa-sūtra."
Therefore, you have no fear whatsoever, nor any fear of an unfortunate rebirth at any time;
your path for traveling to Sukhāvatī has been purified.
For your sake, [I have established] in Sukhāvatī a most magnificent [abode], adorned with divine ornaments and providing the excellent enjoyment of divine nectar.
Having thus comforted those who have cast off their bodies, the lords of sages shall lead them to Sukhāvatī and establish them upon the throne of the Lord Amitābha.
There, having joyfully drunk the nectar of the Dharma from the Lord Amitābha and having taken up the vow of the conduct of awakening, they shall always practice it.
Having gradually fulfilled the equipment for enlightenment for the welfare of the world,
and having attained the threefold awakening, they shall reach perfect nirvana.
Thus has it been fully proclaimed by all the Sugatas;
having heard what I have heard, you all should likewise rejoice in it.
If you all thus desire to go to nirvāṇa,
take refuge in the Three Jewels and observe the poṣadha vow.
Having heard the supreme *Kāraṇḍavyūha*, the king of Mahāyāna sūtras, and always maintaining it with concentration, one practices the vow of awakening.
By the power of this merit, may they always enjoy great bliss;
free from afflictions, pure in nature, and with the three spheres completely purified.
Having undertaken the vow of the conduct of awakening, these Bodhisattvas, the Great Beings, wander for the welfare of the world as the protectors of all saṃsāra.
Then, having gone at the end to Sukhāvatī and having enjoyed great happiness there,
you shall hear the true Dharma of Amitābha and practice virtue.
There too, having fulfilled the equipment for awakening in due order and having attained the threefold awakening, you shall reach perfect nirvana.
This has been fully explained by me, if you desire liberation;
having heard it as I have set it forth, practice accordingly at all times.
Having heard what was thus commanded by him, all those asuras agreed,
saying "So be it," and desired to act accordingly.
Then all those Dānavas, desiring the bliss of liberation,
bowed again to that teacher and made this request with great reverence:
O Teacher, having heard what was instructed by you, we have been awakened;
we wish to practice accordingly, so it behoves you to instruct us further.
Having heard what they thus requested, that Lord of the World, who had assumed the form of an asura,
looked upon all those asuras and, addressing them, commanded as follows:
"O honorable Asuras, all of you listen to what I have spoken;
having heard it and expressed your approval, always practice this vow."
At first, having heard the *Kāraṇḍavyūha*, the most excellent and supreme king of all Mahāyāna sūtras, they were awakened and filled with joy.
Having bathed at dawn in the water of a sacred ford, pure in conduct and with their senses subdued, they took refuge in the Three Jewels and meditated upon the Lord Lokeśvara.
Having worshipped according to the ritual with recitations, hymns of praise, and prostrations,
and having satisfied [the deity], they should make a request for the accomplishment of the vow of awakening.
Having thus completed the vow, they should joyfully maintain its observance during the third watch of the night with meals consisting of the five nectars and free from meat.
Thus, always and according to their ability, they should perform the vow according to the prescribed rule every month, specifically on the eighth and fifteenth days.
One should always observe this vow every month,
or at least once a year during the month of Kārtika.
Whatever action is performed during Kārttika, its fruit is most excellent;
it is immeasurable and incalculable, and it shall never perish.
"Thinking thus and maintaining composure, always practice this vow. Having instructed him in this way, he taught the ritual procedure for it.
Then, having accepted what was commanded by the preceptor and having performed it according to the rules, all those asuras constantly observed that vow.
Then all those Dānavas became Bodhisattvas, Mahāsattvas, who dwelt in the four Brahma-abodes and practiced the conduct of the auspicious ones.
Thus, this one of great supernormal knowledge, having awakened even the most difficult-to-tame dānavas through diligent effort, shall establish them on the path to enlightenment.
Thus, the great and vast heap of merit belonging to that Teacher of the World has been described by the Lords of Sages as immeasurable and incalculable.
Thus that Lord of the Three Worlds, Lokeśvara, the Son of the Victor,
beholding the entire world himself, always protects it within existence.
Awakening even the most wicked and the most difficult to tame through various efforts, and having thus established them on the path to enlightenment, he sends them forth into perfect nirvana.
Therefore, that Teacher of the three worlds, the sovereign lord of all the world,
should always be venerated with devotion by those who desire the wisdom of perfect enlightenment.
Those who, having uttered his name, remembered him, meditated upon him, and worshipped him,
will surely attain enlightenment and reach final liberation.
Having heard this instruction from the Lord of Sages, Ratnapāṇi was awakened;
with a serene mind, he and his attendants rejoiced.
Thus was the greatness of Lokeśvara and his exceedingly vast mass of merit instructed by the Śikhin Buddha, as I heard it from him.
Thus, having recollected the exceedingly great mass of merit of that Lord of the World, and having uttered His name and meditated upon Him, one should always worship Him.
Those who, having uttered his name, remember him, meditate upon him, and worship him—
all those pure-souled ones shall go to Sukhāvatī.
There, having always drunk the nectar of the Dharma from the Lord Amitābha and having taken up the vow of the conduct of awakening, they move about for the welfare of the world.
Bodhisattvas possessing great supernormal powers, whose three spheres are completely purified,
shall attain the threefold enlightenment and reach the state of nirvana.
Having heard these instructions given by the Lord of Munis, Śrīghana, that attendant Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin rejoiced.
Thus concludes the chapter entitled "The Propagation of the True Dharma that Awakens All Aspects of Everything."
6. The Chapter on Awakening the Dānavas Who Are Difficult to Subdue and Introducing Them to the Bodhisattva Conduct.
Then Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, that son of the Conqueror, having bowed once more to the Blessed One, the Lord of Sages, spoke as follows:
"O Blessed One, it is difficult to obtain a vision of that Lord of the World,
and likewise, it is always difficult to hear the True Dharma even within the three realms."
"When will that Lord of the Three Worlds, the Sovereign of the World, come here?
O Teacher, I wish to see that Lord, the Master of All."
Having heard what was thus spoken by him, the Blessed One, that Lord of Sages,
looked toward the Great Being Viṣkambhin and commanded him as follows:
Furthermore, I shall speak of the greatness of the qualities of the True Dharma belonging to that Great-Souled Lord of the World, the Sustainer of the Universe; listen to it with reverence.
On this island there is a delightful ground made of gold,
where many thousands of the enemies of the gods used to dwell.
There, the Lord of the World, the Master of the Three Worlds, beholding them,
proceeded to uplift the wicked and unrestrained demons.
He saw those great evildoers wandering in the ten unwholesome paths,
blinded by intoxication, pride, and excessive arrogance, their hearts tormented by the fire of the afflictions.
Perceiving this, that compassionate one, impelled by loving-kindness and pity,
emitted a ray of merit and approached, illuminating [the world].
Touched by those rays, they were all endowed with happiness;
their minds filled with an extraordinary sense of wonder, they reflected as follows:
"Aha! From where has this splendor come that it has been extended here?
Touched by it, we have all become endowed with great happiness."
As they were reflecting thus, that Lord of the World, the Son of the Conqueror,
appeared before them in the form of a teacher and attended to them.
Seeing him thus approached, all those asuras, being highly pleased, came together, bowed down, and spoke as follows:
Welcome to you; may it be auspicious for you. May you be victorious here, O true Guru!
Enter this seat, O Teacher, and command whatever task must be done.
Having heard this request made by them, he sat down upon his seat;
then, looking at all those who were seated around him, he spoke as follows.
"Whose splendor is this that has arrived, by which such great happiness has come upon us? What do you think—that some wonder is being produced here?"
Having heard what was thus spoken by him, all those Dānavas also,
looking toward their teacher, replied with respect as follows.
"O Teacher, we do not know whose radiance this has come from;
therefore, you ought to instruct us and enlighten us."
Having heard this request from them and having looked at them all, the teacher, seeing that they were desirous of asking about that marvel, spoke thus:
Listen, for I shall speak of that from which this splendor has come;
having heard what I have declared, you ought to act accordingly.
Having heard what was thus commanded by him, all those asuras,
with hearts full of serene faith, bowed to that guru and spoke as follows:
"O Teacher, since you are our instructor and the teacher of the Dharma,
it is right that you should explain this marvelous occurrence which has arisen."
Thus being entreated by them, the Teacher,
beholding all of them filled with wonder and having been propitiated, gave this instruction:
Listen now, all of you, to everything that was spoken by me there;
thus, in order to awaken [you], I shall proclaim that which has arisen as a marvel.
Namely: he who is the Lord of the World, the Sovereign of the entire triple world, the Teacher of the World, the Sustainer of the World, the Bodhisattva, the Son of the Victors.
The Great Being, possessed of great supernormal knowledges, the Noble Avalokiteśvara,
whose nature is pure through loving-kindness and patience, is the Lord composed of compassion.
That glorious Lord of the Three Worlds, the sun of the merit of the True Dharma,
wanders even through the three realms of existence in order to deliver all sentient beings.
Beholding all beings everywhere and awakening them,
he establishes them on the path to enlightenment and sends them to Sukhāvatī.
Thus, he beheld all beings throughout all worlds— even those who were sinful, wicked, and submerged in the hells.
Having touched them with the moons of merit, he uplifted and awakened them.
Having established them on the path to enlightenment, he sends them to Sukhāvatī.
Day after day, beholding them, uplifting them, and awakening them,
he sends immeasurable and incalculable beings to a happy rebirth.
Having acted thus, that Lord of the World, endowed with great merit,
became the sovereign of all phenomena, the Teacher, the King of Dharma, and the Lord of the universe.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, who bears the welfare and benefit of all sentient beings,
is the steadfast lord of all vidyās, a sun of the wisdom of perfect enlightenment.
Having arrived here as well, he shall awaken all sentient beings,
establish them on the path to enlightenment, and send them forth to Sukhāvatī.
Thus, emitting rays of merit here,
illuminating the world of beings, may he travel to the abodes of the Victors.
The splendor of his merit’s radiance has been extended here as well;
touched by it, you are endowed with great happiness.
Having made him your refuge, having meditated upon him, and having remembered him at all times,
you ought to worship him by reciting even his name and bowing down.
Those who, having taken refuge in him, meditate upon and remember him with reverence, and who likewise worship him by devoutly uttering his name, praising him, and bowing down;
None of them are ever born in the miserable realms;
always reborn in happy states, they always practice what is virtuous.
They have ceased the wandering of Māra, are longing for the qualities of the true Dharma,
and desire the vow of awakening that brings about the welfare of all sentient beings.
They were enthusiastic in honoring the Three Jewels, abiding in the four sublime abodes,
elevated by the excellence of auspicious glory and virtues, and devoted to true qualities.

Having enjoyed happiness for as long as life lasts, those who are intent on the welfare of themselves and others should maintain the vow of the conduct of awakening and move through the world for its benefit.
Then, at the conclusion of that time, that very Lord of the World appeared before them face-to-face.
Having approached, one should give consolation, speaking thus before him:
Do not fear, son of good family; there is nothing here for you to fear anywhere.
Having made offerings to the Three Jewels, whatever true Dharma you have acquired,
you shall never again go anywhere among the miserable states;
always born into noble lineages, you shall be endowed with the glory and happiness of the true Dharma.
Having made an offering to the Three Jewels, you should proceed in perfect self-restraint.
Likewise, as long as he practices the vow of the conduct of awakening in this world,
having brought about the welfare and happiness of sentient beings and enjoyed them, he shall at last go to heaven.
There too, O auspicious one, you shall always move about after having enjoyed great happiness.
Thinking thus, always maintaining composure and recollecting the Three Jewels, we remain here; do not despair, for even in death you shall obtain true happiness.
For all living beings in saṃsāra, death is certain;
you, however, having abandoned this body with ease, shall attain a divine one.
Having enjoyed himself as he pleases for as long as he lives together with the immortals in heaven,
he shall thereafter proceed with ease to Sukhāvatī at the end.
Having gone there, take refuge in the Three Teachers of Amitābha;
and having always drunk the nectar of the Dharma, may you proceed in perfect self-restraint.
Having enjoyed there for a very long time the festive joy of the glory of the True Dharma,
you shall finally attain enlightenment and achieve perfect nirvana.
At the end of that time, the Lord of the World, having appeared before them in person, will grant them consolation and bestow fearlessness.
Thus has the truth been fully proclaimed by all the lords of sages;
it has been heard by me as they proclaimed it, and having heard it, one should rejoice and practice accordingly.
Thinking thus, having gone for refuge to this Lord of the Three Worlds,
remember his name, utter it, meditate upon him, and worship him at all times.
In this way, may there always be auspiciousness for you, free from calamity and certain;
having enjoyed happiness throughout your life, may you go at the end to the abode of the gods.
Having enjoyed there for a very long time the festival of happiness consisting of divine desires,
you will then, at the time of your end, pass away and go to Sukhāvatī.
Having gone there, you will always remain in the presence of Amitābha;
having drunk the merit of the nectar of the Dharma, you shall practice with great enthusiasm.
"Even there, after enjoying the great festival of the glory of the True Dharma for a very long time,
you shall finally attain perfect enlightenment and reach final liberation.
Having heard this instruction from him, all those asuras—
Having acknowledged this with "So be it," and having been thus awakened, they spoke as follows.
"O Teacher, we shall act exactly as you have now instructed;
from this day forward, we have always gone for refuge to that Protector."
Having remembered, meditated upon, and recited even the name of that Lord of the World, we offer our salutations; therefore, for our benefit, may you [speak] concerning Him.
"He ought to instruct us also in the rules for the vow.
Having heard this request from them, and seeing that all those Dānavas were unenlightened, the teacher instructed them once more as follows:
Listen, for I shall describe to you the procedure for this vow in brief.
First, having bathed in the water at a sacred ford, pure in conduct and with senses subdued,
having become dwellers in the divine abodes and observed the poṣadha vow,
having gone for refuge to the Three Jewels and meditated upon that Son of the Sugata, they proceeded.
Having invoked and worshipped Lokeśvara according to the prescribed rite,

and having praised him with the *Jagatstotra* and other hymns, one should also perform circumambulation; having praised him with the *Jagatstotra* and other hymns, one should also perform circumambulation.
Having performed the eight-limbed prostration and having recollected [the deity] with deep reverence.
Having uttered the names, and having seen or even heard of his virtues, and having spoken praise and proclaimed it everywhere;
Having honored him with faith and all available offerings,
having worshipped according to one's ability and paid homage, one should worship the Unborn;
thus, having composed oneself daily at the four junctions of the day.
Worship him according to your ability, meditating upon him and remembering him with devotion.
Worship [the deity] always, whether once every day, or even once every month on the eighth or the full moon day of the bright fortnight.
Having performed such deeds as these, all of you, endowed with these virtues,
will surely attain the fruit as described and reach final liberation.
Having heard what was thus commanded by him, all those asuras, being awakened, rejoiced and desired to act accordingly.
Then all those Dānavas, difficult to subdue and arrogant with pride, their hearts overflowing with joy at this abundant and virtuous happiness, [spoke].
Pure in conduct and serene, they longed for the virtues of the true Dharma;
having desisted from wandering through expedient means, they dwelt in the four divine abidings.
Having respectfully undertaken exactly as instructed by that Teacher,
he joyfully took refuge in that Lord of the Three Worlds.
Having meditated and recollected [the deity], always reciting the name according to the ritual procedure,
and having observed the *poṣadha* and the vows, they practiced with concentrated minds.
Having worshipped according to their ability with all available offerings,
having performed circumambulations and prostrations repeatedly,
and having paid homage with the eight limbs, they worshipped and practiced accordingly.
Thus all those Dānavas practiced tranquility, having conquered their senses;
they were pure in virtue, auspicious in conduct, and dwelt in the four [meditative] abodes.
Having acted for each other's benefit and speaking of the qualities of the true Dharma,
they became partakers of enlightenment, devoted to the vow of the conduct of awakening.
Thus, that teacher, awakening all those Dānavas and establishing them on the path to enlightenment, took his leave of them and then departed.
Then, having vanished from that place, Lokeśvara remained stationed in the sky, illuminating everything on all sides; assuming his own form, he revealed it to them all.
Seeing that Lord of the World, the son of the Conqueror, shining in the sky,
all those dānavas were filled with wonder.
Having paid homage there and joyfully gone for refuge to him,
they praised him with recitations, hymns, and the like, and having prostrated, they spoke thus.
Homage to you, O Blessed Lord! We remain forever established in your refuge;
having taken up the vow of the conduct of awakening, may you be gracious toward us as we practice it.
Whatever offense we have committed, that should always be forgiven by you;
thus, having looked upon us, you ought to protect us.
Thus all those asuras, having made their request with great reverence and having bowed to him with the eight limbs, remained gazing upon him.
Then that Lord of the Three Worlds, having bestowed upon them the blessing of victory,
vanished from that place and proceeded elsewhere to deliver sentient beings.
Then all those Dānavas, once again intensely longing for the Dharma, took refuge in the Three Jewels and always proceeded toward what is auspicious.
Thus, that Lord of the Three Worlds, awakening beings through various forms,
diligently establishes even the most difficult to tame in the True Dharma.
Therefore, the lords of sages have declared that the mass of merit of this Lord of the Three Worlds is exceedingly great, immeasurable, and incalculable.
Thus this teacher of the three worlds, the sovereign lord of all the worlds,
has always been praised with devotion by all the omniscient Sugatas.
Thus, having heard his virtuous and glorious account of the world, the people of the world expressed their approval and praised him from all sides.
Thinking thus, those who seek happiness should always remain in refuge with faith in that Lord of the World, the Master of the Universe, and worship him.
Thus was it declared by the One with the Crest (Śikhin), the Perfectly Awakened One, as heard by me;
so have I related it to you here—having heard this, may you awaken accordingly.

Having thus understood its greatness, those who desire the virtues of the True Dharma should always perform [this practice] with devotion, having meditated upon it and recollected it with sincere intent.
Those who, having taken refuge in him, contemplate and remember him with devotion,
and who always joyfully recite even his name—
they all become pure-souled ones, mines of the glorious qualities of a Perfect Buddha.
Having heard this instruction given by the Teacher, the Lord of Sages, they [realized]: "The Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas, shall become the sons of the Jinas."
All of them, headed by Viṣkambhin, being thus awakened, offered their joyful praise.
Thus ends the chapter on awakening the Dānava Durdānta and introducing him to the practice of awakening (*Bodhicaryāvatāra*).
7. The Chapter on Rescuing Beings with Downcast Faces.
Then the Blessed One, the Teacher, the Glorious One, the Master of the Three Worlds, looking toward the Great Being Viṣkambhin, spoke as follows:
Furthermore, noble sons, I have heard of the great qualities of this Lokeśvara; I shall speak of them accordingly, so listen with respect.
Just as in the past there was the Teacher, the Tathāgata, the Lord of Sages,
the Omniscient One, the Arhat, the Great Possessor of Higher Knowledges, the King of Dharma, the Guide;
The Lord who is sovereign over all phenomena, the master of all vidyādharas,
he is the Fully Awakened One named Viśvabhū, the Blessed One, the Sugata, the Victor.
Then, noble sons, I was renowned as a teacher of patience;
I was a great seer, an ascetic, wise, self-controlled, and one who had conquered his senses.

Taking refuge in a mountain cave, he practiced for the sake of attaining the Dharma of perfect enlightenment; dwelling there, he acted for the benefit of sentient beings while abiding in the four divine abodes.
Even then, I heard Viśvabhū proclaiming the exceedingly great power of the qualities of this Teacher of the World, the Lord of the World.
Just as that Teacher of the World, the Blessed One, the Victorious Jina Viśvabhū,
dwelt together with his Saṅgha in that delightful forest hermitage.
Then that Blessed One, residing there in the assembly of all the worlds,
taught the true Dharma and inspired sentient beings toward awakening.
At that time, the Blessed One, that Lord of Sages,
took his seat upon the assembly throne there in order to teach the Noble Dharma.
Then, a great radiance, having illuminated everything all around and brought auspiciousness everywhere, descended, bringing joy.
Touched by those rays, all sentient beings were endowed with happiness;
beholding that wonder, they were filled with amazement.
Then the great-minded Bodhisattva named Gaganagañja,
seeing all those people filled with wonder, arose.
Wearing his upper robe and with palms joined in reverence before him,
he bowed to that Lord of Sages, Viśvabhū, and questioned him in this way.
"Blessed One, whose merit-bestowing radiance has arrived that,
when touched by it, these worlds are endowed with such great happiness?"
Having beheld the Blessed One, the Lord of Sages, they were struck with wonder;
desiring to hear the cause of that, they all stood there with concentrated minds.
Therefore, teach us this cause for dispelling that great wonder and curiosity residing within their hearts: "To whom does this belong?"
Having heard what was thus spoken by him, Viśvabhū, that lord of sages,
looked upon that Great Being Gaganagañja and said:
Listen, noble son, to this which has come as a splendor;
